svg.text: Same VFA front-end as VSA-Flow (You et al., arXiv:2405.08300, 2025), repurposed from optical flow to per-pixel segmentation.
1 · Encoder — HD feature descriptor F (frozen, 0 params)
VSA-Flow convolves the time surface with a Gaussian HD-kernel K± and role-binds polarity/scale (R±, Rˢ).
We use the optimal rank-64 eigen basis of that VFA kernel + FPE on responses — same 0-param, frozen VFA.
designed in encode_pyramid(), finest level in forward()
2 · Bundled matching field Φ + task head
encoder + matcher frozen (requires_grad = False); Adam updates only the head. Loss = cross-entropy (+ optional Dice) vs EVIMO2 mask (ignore 255).
Metrics: IoU / mIoU. ~1.5M trained params total. train.py · seg.py
ADDED · designed, not yet in forward()
This is the piece VSA-Flow does not have and that segmentation specifically needs: it stitches a pixel's descriptor across 50 ms windows into one trajectory
hypervector, so the same moving object keeps one label over time. It is your strongest novelty claim over the flow-only baseline.
Built from: encoder.py · kernel.py · fpe.py · field.py · matching.py · decoder.py · segmentation.py · temporal.py · train.py | Baseline: VSA-Flow, You et al., arXiv:2405.08300 (2025).
